correctness.rationale: The exact published gap recurrences agree after the first gap; the odd first gap on the even Lucas interval gives difference starts (0,1). The source fixes the least exponent at −2j; the upper exponent is 2j, since a nonadjacent finite word headed at e has value in [φ^e,φ^(e+1)), and the interval lies in [φ^(2j),φ^(2j+1)). The span is therefore 4j. Subtracting the recurrences and setting v=u−u_previous gives the stated two nonnegative transitions; v stays at least 1, so u strictly increases at every later gap. Independently checking the envelope: for odd-gap updates the four inequalities reduce, up to shifting k, to (a+1)F_(k+1)+F_k≤F_(k+a+2) and aF_(k+1)+F_k≤F_(k+a+1); the Fibonacci recurrence checks a=0,1,2 and the forward slopes thereafter dominate the left slopes. For even-gap updates, at a=1,2 the four bases follow from F_(k+1)≤2F_k, F_k≤2F_(k−1) for k≥2, and F_(k+2)≥2F_k. At a=2 the four right forward increments are 2F_(k+1), 2F_k, F_(k+3), F_(k+2), respectively, which dominate the slopes F_(k+1), F_(k+1), 2F_k, 2F_k. All later increments are nondecreasing. Initial even span has (1,1) below the envelope, and span 3 is unreachable. The unique difference 1 comes from the two endpoint exponents, giving L_(2j). The sharp witness word has exact sum L_(2j)+F_(2j)=2F_(2j+1) and gaps 1, then j−1 copies of 3, then 1. Before the last gap the difference state is (F_(2j),F_(2j−1)); after it the first coordinate is F_(2j+1). The separate recurrence values before that gap are K_j=F_(2j+1), H_j=F_(2j−1), with K_0=H_0=1 (also consistent with F_(−1)=1 when j=1); applying the last gap gives the two claimed final counts. The nested checks/verify.py and verification notes were read, not executed; they give finite checks, and their sampled uniqueness of the maximum is not asserted or used for the general theorem.

value.rationale: These prior count notions and established Lucas blocks make their discrepancy a motivated invariant. Going from a sign pattern to an exact extremum over every whole block, with a Fibonacci-realizing integer and a span envelope valid over all admissible gaps, gives an independently useful sharp comparison rather than another special-point evaluation.
